title: How to stop forgetting what you read
author: Scott Young
description: The decisive step for long-term retention of what you read occurs long before you open the book. The post How to stop forgetting what you read appeared first on Scott H Young .
summary: Why do we forget so much of what we read in books? In a recent video essay, I explain why what we already know has a much stronger influence on how much we’re able to remember than our intelligence does: Reading More = Reading Better A common confusion I see is the apparent contrast between reading lots of books and reading fewer books more deeply.
takeaways: While somewhat less common, retrieval practice—transforming books and study materials into endless flashcards—can create the same problems.
It is true that reading the same book, multiple times tends to be less effective than practicing retrieval.

When my team and I released a video detailing my AHAB approach to reading more books (the method that helped me get through 105 books during my Foundations project), I got some comments pushing back on the idea of reading so much.
